findings.title: Stale logger name reflects old middleware name
findings.body: The logger passed to `NewLoggerMiddleware` is still named `log.New("plugin.instrumentation")`. Since the instrumentation/metrics logic has been moved out, and this logger is now used by LoggerMiddleware for request completion logs, the name should reflect that (e.g. `plugin.loggermiddleware`) to avoid confusing log output and future maintainers.

findings.title: FromContext silently drops contextual attributes on type-assertion failure
findings.body: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` falls back to `d.New()` (a plain new logger with no context) if the underlying `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` result isn't a `*log.ConcreteLogger`. This silently discards all contextual attributes (e.g. pluginId, dsName, uname) added upstream by `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, meaning log lines from `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` (which relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)`) could lose important plugin/request context without any warning, undermining the stated goal of this PR (moving contextual logging into LoggerMiddleware).

findings.title: No test coverage for new FromContext-based logging behavior
findings.body: `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now depends on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` picking up contextual attributes set by the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, but there is no test added (in this PR) verifying that log output actually contains the pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname attributes that used to be asserted when they lived inside the metrics/instrumentation middleware. The removed fields (pluginId, endpoint, uname, traceID, dsName, dsUID) from `logRequest`'s own params are not covered by any new test demonstrating they are now correctly supplied via context.
